children: is expanding beyond meat substitutes as it seeks to revive growth by targeting consumers focused on protein, health, and weight management, the Wall Street Journal reported.

The company recently introduced products including Beyond Starmatter protein powder, Beyond Starcut meat-free snack bars, and Beyond Immerse, a range of protein-focused carbonated drinks. It is also developing a broader brand strategy around what Chief Executive Officer Ethan Brown calls a “phytosphere,” or plant-based ecosystem.

removed the word “meat” from its packaging last year and has begun using the corporate name Beyond the Plant Protein Company in some communications. The company is also working with marketing agencies on a campaign and new brand positioning planned for next year.
Brown said the brand remains in recovery after years of criticism surrounding plant-based foods, while the company has also faced persistent financial pressure. Beyond
has posted an operating loss every year since its 2019 initial public offering, while its shares have fallen more than 98%.
Revenue declined 8% year over year in the second quarter, an improvement from a 20% drop in the final quarter of 2025.

The company plans to emphasize health and performance, using athletes, bodybuilders, and dietary influencers to promote its products as it seeks to turn consumer interest in protein into sustained demand, the WSJ reported.

title: Beyond Meat broadens product lineup as it seeks to revive sales
